_note: 2026 general-election candidates for State Senate and State House (Nebraska's Legislature) in Nebraska, South Dakota, Idaho, Montana, Alaska and Rhode Island, read from each state's official candidate list on 2026-10-28. "rows" are new cmp-data.js candidate rows (candidate: true; they open no board). "alreadyHeld" are sitting legislators running for the seat they hold: their shell is the row. "crossSeat" are sitting legislators running for a different legislative seat: their shell is untouched and window.CMP_CANDIDACIES carries the candidacy. Withdrawn candidates and write-ins not printed on the ballot are excluded (see each state's note). Montana prints names in capitals; display names of new Montana candidates were converted to title case and may differ from the candidate's own capitalisation (nameAsFiled keeps the source). Rhode Island's candidate file predates its September 9, 2026 primary, so its nominees are the file's filers matched to the Board of Elections' official primary results (most votes in each primary), plus independents the file marks qualified; a withdrawal after July 30, 2026 would not be reflected.

ne.note: Nebraska SOS "Final Statewide General Candidate List 9/11/2026" (Nov 3, 2026 General Election) PDF; "For Member of the Legislature" entries (unicameral, nonpartisan; party column blank). 46 candidates in 25 districts (even-numbered districts plus District 41). Some districts have a single candidate. Chamber recorded as statesenate for the unicameral Legislature.

sd.note: SD SOS "2026 General Election Candidate List" (eid=774), fetched 2026-10-28 via the page's CSV export. Excluded 2 withdrawn: Tom Pischke (R, Senate 25, withdrawn 7/28/2026) and Carl J. Petersen (D, House 28A, withdrawn 6/11/2026). House districts 26A/26B/28A/28B are single-member; other House districts elect 2. Names include nicknames in quotes as printed. Party labels are abbreviations (REP/DEM/IND/LIB).

id.note: Idaho SOS Candidate Filing Portal (run.voteidaho.gov), public candidate search backed by POST https://api-run.voteidaho.gov/api/FiledCandidates/SearchCandidates; election "11/03/2026 - 2026 GENERAL", isFinalList=true, fetched 2026-10-28. Kept filingStatus Approved, non-write-in. Excluded 5 withdrawn: John H Garrett (D, Sen 8), Brenda H. Quick (D, Sen 21), Anna Germana Scholes (I, Sen 24), Emily Fisher (D, House 23A), Enrique Salas Viernes (D, House 24B).

mt.note: Montana SOS candidate filing list for "FEDERAL GENERAL 2026 (11/03/2026) (General)" (e=450002987), fetched 2026-10-28 via CSV export; includes State Senator (25 districts) and State Representative (100 districts). Names printed in ALL CAPS; leading "*" (incumbent marker) stripped from nameAsFiled; display names auto proper-cased (check Mc/Mac/De-style capitalization). Excluded 3 WITHDRAWN (Dave Von Eschen HD22, Jordan Viegut HD57, Deborah Anne Hansen HD77) and 3 declared write-in candidates (not printed on ballot): NATE WHITE (STATE SENATOR DISTRICT 9); ELIJAH TIDSWELL (STATE SENATOR DISTRICT 22); CARI LYNN OLSON (STATE SENATOR DISTRICT 22).

ak.note: Alaska Division of Elections "2026 General Election" candidate list (page last updated September 25, 2026), paginated over 3 pages; all listed candidates marked (Certified). Party labels as printed (e.g. "Registered Republican", "Nonpartisan", "Undeclared"). Senate seats up: A,C,E,G,I,K,M,O,Q,S; all 40 House districts. Excluded certified write-in candidates (not printed on ballot): Darbous, Angela (HOUSE DISTRICT 13); Short, Sarah D. (HOUSE DISTRICT 13).

ri.note: Built from two official sources: (1) RI SOS Candidates.xlsx (HTTP Last-Modified 2026-07-30, i.e. pre-primary; its primary-winner/general-ballot columns are not filled for primary candidates), and (2) RI Board of Elections official results of the 9/9/2026 Statewide Primary (isOfficialResults=true, as of 2026-09-15). Primary candidates: kept Valid+qualified (QBP=Yes) filers only if they won their party primary (top vote-getter; 22 contested legislative primaries, no ties; all uncontested nominees also appear in the results). Independents: kept rows filed for the 11/03/2026 general with QBP=Yes and ON E.B=Yes; excluded independents Peder A Schaefer (Sen 3) and James D Purcell (Sen 19), not marked qualified. nameAsFiled = xlsx First Middle Last Suffix; name = ballot name from primary results (incumbent "*" removed) for nominees, else composed from xlsx. CAVEAT: the xlsx predates the primary, so any post-July-30 withdrawals or party vacancy substitutions after the primary would not be reflected; no official RI general-election candidate list could be fetched (vote.sos.ri.gov HTML and sos.ri.gov/elections pages are behind a Cloudflare challenge, 403).
